subject: Retroactive tier restructure request — Novapulse
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@novapulse.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: retroactive tier restructure for Q4 commitment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Novapulse is seeing a faster-than-expected uplift in usage after the pilot ramp — great news for both teams. That said, our procurement team is asking if Redwood can reclassify ~40% of our November usage into the committed tier for Q4 (effectively a retroactive tier swap) to preserve the originally projected unit economics for finance.

Specifically we are requesting:
- Move 120,000 tokens of usage from on-demand into the committed tier for the Nov 1–30 billing period.
- Apply a one-time usage credit to cover the delta in overruns while we finalize a longer-term committed increase.

I attached a reconciled usage export and our proposed rate table for reference (Novapulse_AE_Rate_Table_v2.xlsx). We understand this is an exception ask; we are prepared to sign a one-year commitment increase (details in attached manifest) if leadership can approve an onetime credit and retroactive tiering for November.

We need a response by end of week to close procurement and avoid a PO delay. Happy to jump back on a short call.

Thanks,
Jake Turner
Head of Strategic Ops — Novapulse

Kimberly / team,

I agree we should be pragmatic here. Quick thoughts:
- Commercial upside: Novapulse is willing to sign a 12-month commit that ups MRR by ~35% starting Jan. If they deliver on that, the one-time hit is recovered within 2–3 months.
- Proposed concession (sales view): offer a retroactive reclassification for Nov up to 120k tokens and a one-time credit equal to the difference between on-demand and committed rate for those tokens, capped at $28k. In exchange: execute the 12-month commitment by COB Dec 3 + payment of the first month upfront.
- Ask: we need finance to confirm the cash/margin impact and approval to offer a capped credit.

I can take lead on contract paperwork and getting the signature if we have the green light.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: retroactive tier restructure for Q4 commitment — finance calc

Team,

I ran the numbers based on the attached usage manifest. Summary:
- Requested retroactive volume: 120,000 tokens (Nov).
- On-demand rate: $0.012 /k token (example), Committed tier rate: $0.009 /k token.
- Delta credit = 120k * ($0.012 - $0.009) = $360 (note: numbers are scaled — see attachment for full decimal breakdown).
- However, the expected expanded commit (if signed) increases annual ARR by ~$420k; NPV positive.

My ask for executive approval:
1) Approve offering a capped one-time credit not to exceed $30k (to cover any reconciliation differences and ancillary fees).
2) Approve retroactive reclassification of up to 120k tokens for November only, contingent on a signed 12-month commitment and first-month upfront payment by Dec 3.

Rationale: customer retention + ARR upside outweighs the one-time hit, but we should document as a precedent exception and put a strict cap. Also recommend Finance keep a serialized exception register for audit.

Attaching a short memo with line-item calc.

-Markus
Markus Klein
